owner.occupation: Hand bookbinder running a two-person atelier in the 11th arrondissement

world.bio: Hand bookbinder in Paris, 11th arrondissement. Two-person atelier (me and Jules, my assistant), trained at a Paris bookbinding school, now binding limited editions for collectors and small presses. I like rounded spines, linen thread and paste that smells of wheat. Evenings I go hunting for unusual cover cloth in flea markets, fabric stores in the Marais and on the internet when my eyes allow.
skills_assets: Fine binding: full leather, half cloth, Coptic, Japanese stab
Hand tools: Dutch bone folders, a 1930s lying press, a Schärfmaschine that I adore
A list of 20 collectors and small presses who send commissions
Relationship with a gilder in the 18th and a marbler in Montreuil
Atelier of 38 square metres, one window onto a courtyard with a fig tree
Knows exactly what the Geneva collector's cover needs: roughly 4 metres in total of woven indigo silk for the 40-copy run

projects.name: Collector's poetry edition, 40 copies
projects.text: A collector in Geneva commissioned forty copies of a poetry edition (a contemporary Occitan poet, printed letterpress in Lyon) and wants a woven silk cover, hand-dyed in a deep indigo with a fine herringbone pattern. I worked out about 4 metres in total, allowing for waste. Delivery of the finished copies is set for mid-February. I wrote to mills in Lyon and Como; both quoted minimums of 100 metres, which makes no sense for 4.

projects.name: Restoring a 1920s guestbook
projects.text: Hotel in Deauville commissioned the repair of a guestbook with broken hinges. Many famous signatures. Slow work, mostly paste and patience.

projects.name: Workshop for students
projects.text: Thinking about two-day workshops in the atelier for beginners, perhaps in spring, to cover rent.

notes.text: Jules glued a title page upside down again. We laughed, then I felt guilty because we had to reprint it. Third time this year, but his sewing is getting very clean.
Marché aux puces de Vanves. Found two metres of faded indigo velvet, not silk, not woven. No. But my heart skipped. Bought it anyway, 12 euros.
Letter from the mill in Lyon: 100m minimum per colour. I'm paying for four. Wrote back politely. They wrote back politely. We both lost.
Daughter Manon called from Lyon, she hates her first stats course. I said it gets better. It does not always get better.
Food bank on Saturday, sorted tins and cooked rice for 80. The line is longer than in spring. A man asked if I did books and I said yes, mostly old ones. He said 'those are the best.'
Peugeot bicycle: new Brooks saddle, old chain finally replaced. Rode along the canal Saint-Martin at 7am. The city is quiet in a way I love.
Cut leather for the Deauville guestbook. Using a 1.2mm calf skin, tanned in Annonay. Smell of leather is the smell of my father's workshop.
Collector in Geneva emailed asking about progress. I said 'cover cloth is in progress'. That is a kind way to say 'I don't have the cloth'.
Visited a shop on rue du Faubourg Saint-Antoine for threads. They had seven kinds of silk twill, none woven in the pattern. The woman said 'ask a small weaver, not a mill.'

messages.text: Jules: Mills still no? Me: No. They want 100 metres. Jules: That's like 25 books worth. Me: It's 40 copies. Jules: Right, so 4 metres. Me: Yes, 4. Jules: Maybe a small workshop that does samples? Me: Maybe.
Manon: Maman, I think I want to change to design. Me: Do you want to or are you scared? Manon: Both. Me: Then wait until Christmas.
M. Aubry: Dear Hélène, I'm very keen on the indigo silk we discussed. Is it possible? Me: Yes, I'm sourcing now. Aubry: February is firm. Me: Understood.
Étienne: I can do 20 sheets of marbling for you in two weeks. Me: Wonderful, can you do indigo? Étienne: I do what the bath wants.

Call with M. Aubry on cover cloth update
Drive to Lyon to see the letterpress printer and pick up signatures

relations.about: Daughter, first year at a university in Lyon, anxious.
Geneva collector, meticulous, pays on time.

constraints: The cover must be woven silk, nothing printed
Maximum price for cloth about 180 euros per metre
sensitive: Rent of the atelier is going up 12 percent in January
Her husband left four years ago and she still reorganises her bookshelf when stressed
Worried about her daughter's mental health
